properties.name: MEASURED 2026-09-23: re-declaring an existing dependency with external_dependency REPLACES the Resource node and silently drops its `description` — a 3,015-character history on flo2's dep:reflow2 vanished
properties.source: who:claude-code, re-pinning flo2's dep:reflow2 from v0.66.0 to v0.67.0 with the v0.67.0 release binary; get_node before and after
properties.statement:
WHAT WAS OBSERVED. flo2's `dep:reflow2` (a Resource, resource_type design-dependency) carried a 3,015-character `description`: the record of every earlier re-declaration and what each stale pin had cost. Re-declaring it at v0.67.0 with `external_dependency` (id, name, source, version, features, design_export, design_export_seen_at — no description, because the tool has no such parameter) returned success. Immediately afterwards `get_node` showed NO `description` property at all, and `replace_text` on it was refused naming the text properties the node now had, none of them `description`.

EXPECTED. Revising a node elsewhere in reflow2 keeps what the call omits — `add_resource`, `add_artifact` and the other constructors say so in their own descriptions ("omitted fields keep their stored value"). `external_dependency`'s description says a re-declare takes "a new baseline", which reads as moving the version and the watched export, not as discarding the node's prose.

NOT AFFECTED. `add_resource` on the same node with only `id` and `description` restored the text and kept every dependency field (version, features, design_export_hash) — so the node type holds both happily; it is the re-declare path that does not preserve.

IMPACT. The recurring job this tool exists for — re-pinning when upstream moves, which `loop_status` nags about on every release — erases whatever a project wrote about its dependency, with a success reply. flo2 caught it only because the next call targeted that field. Recovered here from the committed export; a project that re-exported first would have committed the loss. Not established: whether other properties outside the tool's parameter list are dropped the same way (only `description` was present to lose), or whether the revision guard's preserved-on-write snapshot captured the prior state.

SAME TOOL, SECOND LOSSY SHAPE — MEASURED 2026-09-24 on flo2's move to v0.70.0: `external_dependency` stores `features` as ONE comma-joined string, so a feature whose text contains a comma comes back as several. "the jot skill: /jot, /note and /log-issue, the word is the tag (0.70.0)" was stored and echoed as three features ("the jot skill: /jot", "/note and /log-issue", "the word is the tag (0.70.0)"), and the dependency manifest the call returns shows the split. Worked around by re-declaring with a comma-free wording. Nothing refuses or warns; a caller only sees it by reading the echoed manifest. Found from the dev_reflow2 hub session.

RECURRED 2026-09-26 ON 0.71.0, SIX TIMES IN ONE dev_reflow2 HUB SESSION — AND ONE "NOT ESTABLISHED" ABOVE IS NOW MEASURED (appended; nothing above changed). The hub re-declared dep:reflow2 three times (e411c84; e411c84+uncommitted@sha256:2a727919; 5f41b35) and dep:flo2 three times (3a825be; 3a825be+uncommitted@sha256:7d8407e6; d2221f3). Every re-declare dropped the Resource's description, 2 to 4 KB of per-pin history. Every one was restored with add_resource in the next call, re-sending the whole text; the restore worked each time and kept the new version and hash. THE SNAPSHOT QUESTION: the preserved-on-write guard does NOT capture the description a re-declare drops. The hub's export after the first two re-declares showed exactly two nodes changed (dep:flo2 and dep:reflow2: description, version, hash, seen-at) and NO snapshot node added, whereas replace_text and add_resource revisions in the same session each did add one. The only surviving copy of each dropped description was the committed export in git. A re-declare followed by a re-export, before the restore, would have committed the loss.

RECURRED 2026-09-27 ON 0.71.0 (occurrence 7 counted here; appended, nothing above changed). The dev_reflow2 hub re-declared dep:cure by its flo2.io address with no design_export, to retire the file watch under the design-and-export rules. The description (about 3 KB of connection history) dropped as before and was restored with add_resource in the next call. NEW IN THIS ONE: re-declaring with design_export OMITTED also cleared the stored design_export, design_export_hash and design_export_seen_at. That was the effect wanted here, but it is the same replace-not-merge behaviour, so a caller who only meant to move the version would also lose the watch without being told.

UPDATE 2026-09-28: still reproduces on 0.72.0 (scratch store). Re-declaring without `note` dropped the description, because core declare_external_dependency writes with create_node (replace). It is the same mechanism as plan_epoch, in the class recorded in fact:root-cause-the-revise-contract-is-implemented-per-handler-and-guarded-by-instances-2026-09-28.

2026-10-01 — STILL TRUE ON 0.76.0, AND IT RECURRED TWICE IN ONE SESSION. In the dev_reflow2 hub, re-pinning dep:reflow2 (v0.76.0, with design_export moved to a clean worktree) and dep:flo2 (0752a8e, design_address) each dropped the Resource's description: 4,706 and 4,420 characters of history. Each time it was restored with add_resource in the same step, by RE-SENDING the whole text. A script then checked word for word that the restored history matched the committed export, which is the only way to know a hand transcription of ~5 KB was exact. The hub's notes now say "still true on 0.76.0" in both dependencies.
